cues.en: Mike: Welcome to this section of the course, which is all about regression.
cues.zh: Mike：歡迎來到專門介紹迴歸的單元。

cues.en: I'm going to start this course by talking about what a GLM, which stands for general linear model, means in general, and that's going to lead us into a more focused discussion
cues.zh: 先談 GLM，也就是一般線性模型的整體意義，再逐步進入更聚焦的

cues.en: of a regression analysis.
cues.zh: 迴歸分析討論。

cues.en: You'll see that a general linear model is a framework for doing analysis and a regression is one type of general linear model.
cues.zh: 你會看到，一般線性模型是一套分析架構，而迴歸是其中一種類型。

cues.en: So there is a concept in statistics and data modeling that I introduced in the first lecture of the section on hypothesis testing.
cues.zh: 假設檢定單元第一堂，介紹過統計與資料建模中的一個概念。

cues.en: And that is that we have our data, which is just a bunch of numbers that are measured from the world somehow, and we have a model, which is a set of mathematical equations that we define,
cues.zh: 我們有資料，也就是以某種方式從世界量測到的一組數字，也有模型，也就是自行定義的數學方程式，

cues.en: and the idea is we want to match the model to the data and see how well the model fits the data.
cues.zh: 目標是讓模型與資料吻合，看看模型擬合資料的程度。

cues.en: Now, we can break down this model conceptually into two additional parts.
cues.zh: 概念上，模型還能分成兩部分。

cues.en: So we have the fixed features and the free parameters.
cues.zh: 固定特徵與自由參數。

cues.en: Fixed features are the components of the model that you as the researcher, you as the data scientist, the data analyst, the statistician, the data engineer,
cues.zh: 固定特徵，是由你這位研究者、資料科學家、資料分析師、統計學家、資料工程師，

cues.en: whatever you wanna call yourself, you get to define these features.
cues.zh: 不管你如何稱呼自己，來定義的模型成分。

cues.en: This is based on theory, on intuition, on what you expect to see in the data.
cues.zh: 基於理論、直覺，以及對資料的預期。

cues.en: And then we have these free parameters, and the idea is that these are the fixed features that are immutable, they're just in the model.
cues.zh: 接著有自由參數；概念是，固定特徵不可改變，會保留在模型裡。

cues.en: And the free parameters are the things that we allow to change numerically depending on how well the model fits the data.
cues.zh: 自由參數則允許依照模型對資料的擬合程度，改變數值。

cues.en: So if we can change these free parameters, allow the data to change the free parameters in order to get the model to fit the data better within the constraints defined by our fixed features,
cues.zh: 如果能調整自由參數，讓資料改變自由參數，在固定特徵的限制內，讓模型更好地擬合資料，

cues.en: then that's great, that's the goal here.
cues.zh: 那就很好，這就是目標。

cues.en: So that's the two parts of a model, the fixed features and the free parameters.
cues.zh: 模型的兩部分，就是固定特徵與自由參數。

cues.en: And the idea is that the fixed features you define a priori, this is what you have control over, and the free parameters are what get tweaked by the data themselves.
cues.zh: 固定特徵由你事先定義，是你能控制的；自由參數則由資料本身調整。

cues.en: You might be wondering, what is the difference between an ANOVA and a regression?
cues.zh: 你可能想知道，ANOVA 與迴歸有什麼差別？

cues.en: And when should you do an ANOVA and when should you use a regression?
cues.zh: 何時應做 ANOVA，何時用迴歸？

cues.en: So this slide explains it.
cues.zh: 這張投影片說明。

cues.en: You use an ANOVA when all of the independent variables are discrete, usually categorical.
cues.zh: 所有自變數都是離散，通常是類別時，使用 ANOVA。

cues.en: But if your independent variables are numeric, then you can discretize them.
cues.zh: 如果自變數是數值，也可以離散化。

cues.en: I showed several examples of this in the previous section, for example, with age, so binning age into young people versus older people.
cues.zh: 上一單元示範過幾個例子，例如把年齡分成年輕與年長。

cues.en: So there I'm turning what is originally a continuous variable into categorical, young versus old.
cues.zh: 把原本的連續變數，轉成年輕、年長的類別。

cues.en: So when all the independent variables are discrete, categorical, then use an ANOVA, and use regression when the independent variables are continuous.
cues.zh: 所以所有自變數都是離散、類別時，用 ANOVA；自變數連續時，使用迴歸。

cues.en: So a regression is kind of like an extension of a correlation.
cues.zh: 迴歸有點像相關的延伸。

cues.en: A correlation is just between two variables, X and Y, and a regression can be extended to multiple variables.
cues.zh: 相關只針對 X 與 Y 兩個變數，迴歸則可以延伸到多個變數。

cues.en: Now, in a regression, you actually can have some of the independent variables be categorical, they need to be dummy-coded.
cues.zh: 迴歸中，其實也可以有部分自變數是類別，但必須做虛擬編碼。

cues.en: You'll see an example of that in a few moments.
cues.zh: 稍後會舉例。

cues.en: But if at least some or at least one of the independent variables is continuous, then you would want to use a regression.
cues.zh: 只要至少部分，或至少一個自變數是連續的，就會想使用迴歸。

cues.en: Okay, so model fitting, in general, has five steps.
cues.zh: 一般而言，模型擬合有五個步驟。

cues.en: Now, I haven't really discussed these five steps earlier in the course, but, in fact, we've kind of been doing something like this anyway previously.
cues.zh: 之前沒有明確討論這五步，但其實前面也一直在做類似的事。

cues.en: So I'll list them here quickly and then I'm gonna spend a few moments talking about each one of these steps.
cues.zh: 先快速列出，再花一些時間討論各步驟。

cues.en: So step one is to define the equations underlying the model.
cues.zh: 第一步，定義模型背後的方程式。

cues.en: Step two is to map the data onto the model equations, and then we convert the equations into a matrix-vector equation, and I'll show what that means in a moment.
cues.zh: 第二步，把資料映射到模型方程式，再把方程式轉成矩陣向量方程式，稍後會示範意思。

cues.en: And then we compute the parameters, this is the kind of statistical analysis part.
cues.zh: 接著計算參數，這就是統計分析的部分。

cues.en: And then we do step five that is the statistical evaluation of the model.
cues.zh: 然後是第五步，對模型進行統計評估。

cues.en: So let's start with discussing step one.
cues.zh: 先討論第一步。

cues.en: So let's say, this is an example that I've given earlier in the course.
cues.zh: 這是課程前面舉過的例子。

cues.en: Let's say we want to have a model that predicts how tall people are as adults.
cues.zh: 假設想建立模型，預測成年後身高。

cues.en: So we have their height, and then we say that someone's height is related to their sex, because in general, men tend to be taller than women,
cues.zh: 有身高，再假設身高與性別有關，因為一般男性傾向比女性高，

cues.en: it's related to their parents' height because people with taller parents tend to be taller themselves, and it's related to childhood nutrition because, yeah, the healthier you are as a child,
cues.zh: 也與父母身高有關，因為父母高的人通常也較高；還與兒童期營養有關，因為小時候愈健康，

cues.en: the more likely you are to be tall as an adult.
cues.zh: 長大後愈可能長得高。

cues.en: So these are the three fixed features, s, p, and n.
cues.zh: 這就是 s、p 與 n 三個固定特徵。

cues.en: So these are the fixed features that I brought into the model, me as the researcher, I said that these are the three features that I want in the model.
cues.zh: 由我作為研究者，帶入模型，決定要納入這三個特徵。

cues.en: But the thing is, I don't know how important sex is for height, I don't know how important parent's height is, and I don't know how important childhood nutrition is,
cues.zh: 但我不知道性別、父母身高，以及兒童期營養，對身高各有多重要，

cues.en: so therefore I need to add these flexible features into the model in order for the data to tell me how important childhood nutrition really is.
cues.zh: 所以必須加入這些可調整特徵，讓資料告訴我，兒童期營養究竟有多重要。

cues.en: And that's the idea of these beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 這就是 beta 係數的概念。

cues.en: They're called betas, that's the Greek lowercase character beta, and they're variously called regression coefficients or beta values or beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 它們稱為 beta，是希臘小寫字母 beta，也稱迴歸係數、beta 值，或 beta 係數。

cues.en: And then we have this term called the intercept, and I've mentioned this term intercept previously in this section on ANOVA.
cues.zh: 接著有截距項，之前 ANOVA 單元提過截距。

cues.en: So we need, almost always we need an intercept in our general linear model.
cues.zh: 一般線性模型幾乎總是需要截距。

cues.en: The intercept captures the average height when all the other parameters are zero.
cues.zh: 截距捕捉其他參數都為 0 時的平均身高。

cues.en: So imagine setting beta one to zero, beta two to zero, beta three to zero, so this entire equation just becomes h height equals beta zero.
cues.zh: 假設 beta1、beta2、beta3 全設為 0，整個方程式就變成身高 h 等於 beta0。

cues.en: So then whatever is the value of beta zero is going to be the intercept.
cues.zh: beta0 的值，就是截距。

cues.en: I will talk more about this intercept later on in this video.
cues.zh: 這支影片稍後會再討論。

cues.en: Okay, so here we have our equation, this is our model.
cues.zh: 這是方程式，也就是模型。

cues.en: Now we get to step two, and that is to map the data into the model equation.
cues.zh: 第二步，把資料映射到模型方程式。

cues.en: So we do some research, we do some surveys, and we end up with a data table that looks like this.
cues.zh: 進行研究與調查，得到這樣的資料表。

cues.en: So we have, we measure data from 10 people, we have their height, their sex, their parents' height, maybe this is like the average of their parents, whatever, and childhood nutrition,
cues.zh: 量測 10 個人的身高、性別、父母身高，也許是雙親平均等等，以及兒童期營養，

cues.en: maybe this is like a score from 1 to 10 or something like that.
cues.zh: 也許是 1 到 10 的分數。

cues.en: Okay, now, this table we cannot statistically analyze directly.
cues.zh: 不能直接對這張表進行統計分析。

cues.en: We need to map this table or the data in this table onto the equations that define our model.
cues.zh: 需要把表格或表內資料，映射到定義模型的方程式。

cues.en: So that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 像這樣。

cues.en: This is our model and we treat this like a template, this is like the template model and we weave our actual empirical data into this model.
cues.zh: 把模型當成模板，再把實際經驗資料嵌入模型。

cues.en: So that gives us a set of equations that all look like this, except that h, s, p, and n are replaced
cues.zh: 得到一組都長得像這樣的方程式，但 h、s、p 與 n，會換成

cues.en: with the actual numbers that we measured from the people.
cues.zh: 實際從人身上量測的數字。

cues.en: So this is their height, this is our dependent variable here, and then we have the various independent variables.
cues.zh: 這是身高，也就是依變數，接著有各種自變數。

cues.en: So sex, and here you can see I'm dummy coding, so zero could be for women and one could be for men.
cues.zh: 性別可以看到使用虛擬編碼，0 可以表示女性，1 表示男性。

cues.en: And just a quick reminder about dummy coding.
cues.zh: 快速提醒虛擬編碼。

cues.en: If we set zero to be for females and one to be for males, then we expect this beta coefficient to be positive because males tend to be larger than females.
cues.zh: 女性設為 0，男性設為 1，就預期這個 beta 係數為正，因為男性通常體型較大。

cues.en: Now, we could also dummy-code it the other way.
cues.zh: 也可以反過來編碼。

cues.en: So we could have zero for females, sorry, zero for males and one for females.
cues.zh: 女性設為 0——抱歉，男性設為 0，女性設為 1。

cues.en: And then the beta coefficient, the value itself would be identical, the magnitude would be identical, but now we would expect it to have a minus sign because this would indicate
cues.zh: beta 係數本身的大小、絕對值會相同，但現在預期帶負號，表示

cues.en: that females are less tall than males.
cues.zh: 女性比男性矮。

cues.en: So the female height on average is going to be negative relative to the male height.
cues.zh: 平均而言，女性身高相對於男性會是負的。

cues.en: So you can see that the dummy coding can go either way.
cues.zh: 所以虛擬編碼可以採任一方向。

cues.en: Usually it makes sense to have the thing that you expect to be larger to be a number one so that the beta coefficient is positive, it just makes things a little bit easier
cues.zh: 通常，把預期較大的類別設為 1，讓 beta 係數為正，會讓大多數情況下的解讀

cues.en: to interpret in most cases.
cues.zh: 稍微容易一些。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Anyway, you can see that we've mapped the data onto the model equation, so that is step two.
cues.zh: 總之，已把資料映射到模型方程式，完成第二步。

cues.en: Now step three is to convert these individual equations, one equation for each individual in our dataset, into a matrix-vector equation.
cues.zh: 第三步，把資料集中每個人各自的一條方程式，轉成矩陣向量方程式。

cues.en: Now, this gets a little bit into linear algebra.
cues.zh: 這涉及一些線性代數。

cues.en: So if this step seems a little strange, then don't worry too much about the math.
cues.zh: 如果覺得有點奇怪，不用太擔心數學。

cues.en: The thing is that also with step two and step three, and, in fact, also step four, which I'll show in a moment, you generally don't have to do all this stuff on your own,
cues.zh: 其實第二、第三步，以及稍後展示的第四步，通常都不必自己完成，

cues.en: the computer program is going to do this for you, but it is important for you to understand conceptually what is going on behind the scenes.
cues.zh: 電腦程式會代勞，但概念上理解背後運作，仍然重要。

cues.en: Okay, so what we do is we take all of these equations and we separate out the different parts of the equations, and that gives us a matrix and two vectors.
cues.zh: 取出所有方程式，把不同部分分開，就得到一個矩陣與兩個向量。

cues.en: So this matrix here on the left, you can see this contains all of our independent variables.
cues.zh: 左邊矩陣包含全部自變數。

cues.en: So each row corresponds to a different individual in our dataset and each column corresponds to an independent variable.
cues.zh: 每列對應資料集的一個人，每欄對應一個自變數。

cues.en: So this is the intercept, the sex, parents' height, and childhood nutrition.
cues.zh: 截距、性別、父母身高，以及兒童期營養。

cues.en: And then we have this vector here and this is the vector of beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 接著有這個向量，是 beta 係數向量。

cues.en: These are all the unknown parameters that we wanna fit to the data.
cues.zh: 全部是要配適到資料的未知參數。

cues.en: And then we set that equal to, and then each element in this vector is the dependent variable.
cues.zh: 令它等於這裡，這個向量的各元素是依變數。

cues.en: So I hope that makes sense.
cues.zh: 希望這樣清楚。

cues.en: We have a matrix where all the columns are the independent variables and a vector that corresponds to the dependent variable,
cues.zh: 矩陣各欄都是自變數，另有對應依變數的向量，

cues.en: and then we have a vector of the unknowns, these are the coefficients that we want to solve for in our model fitting.
cues.zh: 以及未知數向量，也就是模型擬合時要求解的係數。

cues.en: Okay, now, we can shorten this.
cues.zh: 可以縮寫。

cues.en: So I'm gonna call this matrix X, this matrix B, but it's a bolded B, just to separate the vector B in bold
cues.zh: 把這個矩陣稱為 X，這個稱為粗體 B，用粗體區分向量 B，

cues.en: from the individual betas that are not bold, and then we have the output, the outcome variables, the dependent variables, and that I'm calling vector y.
cues.zh: 以及非粗體的個別 beta；輸出、結果變數、依變數，則稱為向量 y。

cues.en: So notice these are all bolded letters, that's often used in linear algebra to indicate matrices and vectors.
cues.zh: 注意，全都是粗體，線性代數常用來表示矩陣與向量。

cues.en: So the result of step three is to convert these equations into this compact matrix-vector equation.
cues.zh: 第三步的結果，就是把這些方程式轉成精簡的矩陣向量方程式。

cues.en: Again, this is stuff that most of the time the computer is doing for you unless you feel like implementing all of this stuff on your own in code, which, of course, is also feasible.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，通常電腦會代勞，除非你想自己用程式碼實作，當然也可行。

cues.en: Okay, so then step four is to compute the parameters, that means actually assign numbers, numerical values, to all of those beta coefficients.
cues.zh: 第四步，計算參數，也就是真正替所有 beta 係數指定數字、數值。

cues.en: I'm gonna talk about that in the next lecture, so keep watching to get to that discussion.
cues.zh: 下一堂會談，請繼續看。

cues.en: And then we get to step five, which is the statistical evaluation of the model.
cues.zh: 第五步，是模型的統計評估。

cues.en: And here we're asking two questions.
cues.zh: 這裡問兩個問題。

cues.en: Question one is, is the model itself, the entire model, even a reasonable model?
cues.zh: 第一，整個模型本身是否合理？

cues.en: Is it a good model?
cues.zh: 是不是好模型？

cues.en: Does the model fit the data well?
cues.zh: 模型是否能良好擬合資料？

cues.en: That's not, we're not guaranteed to have a model that even fits the data at all.
cues.zh: 不能保證模型一定能擬合資料。

cues.en: So that's the first question.
cues.zh: 這是第一個問題。

cues.en: Is the model in its entirety a good fit to the data?
cues.zh: 整個模型是否良好擬合資料？

cues.en: And then if the answer is, well, if the answer is no, then go back to the drawing board and try to come up with a better model, or maybe look at the data, see if there's something wrong with the data.
cues.zh: 如果答案是否，就重新構思更好的模型，或查看資料是否有問題。

cues.en: So if the question here is yes, the model is a decent fit to the data, then we go on to step two, which is to ask whether the individual beta coefficients
cues.zh: 如果答案是對，模型擬合得不錯，就進入第二個問題：個別 beta 係數

cues.en: are statistically significant.
cues.zh: 是否達到統計顯著？

cues.en: So let me just remind you of this equation here, this is our model.
cues.zh: 提醒一下這個方程式，就是模型。

cues.en: So step one is just saying, is all of this stuff good?
cues.zh: 第一步只是在問，這整套東西是否好？

cues.en: Everything on the right-hand side of this equation, is that a good, reasonable model of height?
cues.zh: 方程式右側全部內容，是否是合理的身高模型？

cues.en: Now, of course, we don't need to explain every single tiny variance in the scale of nanometers of height, but we just wanna know in general,
cues.zh: 當然，不需要解釋細微到奈米尺度的每一點身高變異，只是想知道，

cues.en: is this a decent way to model the height data?
cues.zh: 整體而言，這是否是合理的身高建模方式？

cues.en: And if that's the case, we can then look at individual coefficients.
cues.zh: 如果是，就能看個別係數。

cues.en: So it might turn out that the model in general is a good model.
cues.zh: 可能模型整體很好。

cues.en: However, let's say childhood nutrition is actually not nearly as important as I thought it was, so it turns out that this beta three
cues.zh: 但假設兒童期營養，其實遠不如我想像的重要，beta3

cues.en: is not statistically significant.
cues.zh: 未達統計顯著。

cues.en: That would mean that this beta three is not statistically distinguishable from zero.
cues.zh: 表示 beta3 在統計上，無法與 0 區分。

cues.en: So that would tell us that although the model fits the data well, this one individual parameter is actually not important, this is not contributing to the model.
cues.zh: 這告訴我們，雖然模型擬合良好，但這一個參數其實不重要，對模型沒有貢獻。

cues.en: Okay, and again, I'm going to talk more about step five in later videos in this section.
cues.zh: 本單元後面會進一步討論第五步。

cues.en: What I want to do now is go back and talk a little bit more about this intercept term here, this beta naught, this beta zero.
cues.zh: 現在回頭多談一點截距項，也就是 beta naught、beta0。

cues.en: So the intercept term needs to be in the model, it captures the offset of the data when all of the other predictors are set to zero.
cues.zh: 截距必須在模型裡，捕捉其他預測變數全設為 0 時，資料的位移。

cues.en: The thing is that the intercept term is usually not very interesting, it's usually not very interpretable, but it usually needs to be in there,
cues.zh: 截距通常不有趣，也不太能解讀，但通常必須存在，

cues.en: so you have to be mindful that your models incorporate a intercept term.
cues.zh: 所以要注意模型是否包含截距。

cues.en: So geometrically, it looks something like this.
cues.zh: 從幾何角度看，像這樣。

cues.en: Imagine that these are our data, so this is two dimensional data.
cues.zh: 假設這些是資料，是二維資料。

cues.en: We have our outcome measure and the independent variable here.
cues.zh: 這裡是結果量測，這裡是自變數。

cues.en: So then we get this nice fit here between our two variables.
cues.zh: 得到兩個變數之間漂亮的擬合線。

cues.en: Okay, so nothing really bizarre here.
cues.zh: 沒有什麼奇怪。

cues.en: Now, if we were to run the same general linear model, the same regression, without having an intercept, that would give this best-fit line, well, quote, unquote, "Best-fit line."
cues.zh: 但如果用相同一般線性模型、相同迴歸，卻沒有截距，就會得到這條「最佳擬合線」。

cues.en: Mathematically, this is the right solution, but obviously when you look at this, you see that this is not a good solution.
cues.zh: 數學上是正確解，但一看就知道並不是好解。

cues.en: So without an intercept, we are forcing all of the predictors to be, or the data to be zero when all predictors are zero, which means that we are forcing this best-fit line
cues.zh: 沒有截距，就是強制所有預測變數——或者說，所有預測變數為 0 時，資料也必須為 0，讓這條最佳擬合線

cues.en: to go through the origin of this graph.
cues.zh: 通過圖的原點。

cues.en: So you can see that that's really not appropriate here.
cues.zh: 可以看出，這裡並不合適。

cues.en: Now, the one case when you do not need an intercept term is if all of your data are mean-centered.
cues.zh: 唯一不需要截距的情況，是所有資料都已平均中心化。

cues.en: So if the average of the dependent variable is zero, if the average of all the independent variables are zero, then the intercept is guaranteed to be zero,
cues.zh: 依變數平均值為 0，所有自變數平均值也為 0，就能保證截距為 0，

cues.en: so then you can leave it out.
cues.zh: 因此可以省略。

cues.en: But that's an exception, so just get it in your head that you always include an intercept term whenever you are running a general linear model
cues.zh: 但這是例外，所以要記住，執行一般線性模型

cues.en: or a regression.
cues.zh: 或迴歸時，總是納入截距。

cues.en: So a little bit of terminology.
cues.zh: 再介紹一些術語。

cues.en: Here we have the general linear model equation, which I've already introduced you to.
cues.zh: 這是已經介紹過的一般線性模型方程式。

cues.en: So we have y equals X times beta, and sometimes this is also written with an epsilon here, which would reflect the errors or the residuals.
cues.zh: y 等於 X 乘 beta，有時還會寫上 epsilon，表示誤差或殘差。

cues.en: I'll talk more about this in a few videos from now.
cues.zh: 幾支影片之後會再談。

cues.en: So this matrix X is called the design matrix.
cues.zh: 矩陣 X 稱為設計矩陣。

cues.en: So the columns are all of your independent variables, which are also sometimes called predictors, also sometimes called regressors.
cues.zh: 各欄都是自變數，有時稱預測變數，也稱迴歸變數。

cues.en: The entire matrix itself is called the design matrix.
cues.zh: 整個矩陣稱為設計矩陣。

cues.en: And then we have beta, so that is the vector of regression coefficients or beta parameters.
cues.zh: beta 是迴歸係數，或 beta 參數的向量。

cues.en: These are the things that we are trying to fit with our regression approach.
cues.zh: 這些就是迴歸方法要擬合的項目。

cues.en: And then we have vector y, which is the dependent variable or the outcome measure or the data, there's just different terms for the same thing.
cues.zh: 向量 y 是依變數、結果量測，或資料，只是同一件事的不同名稱。

cues.en: So I want to talk about the term linear in general linear model.
cues.zh: 想談談一般線性模型中「線性」的意思。

cues.en: There's a reason why the GLM has linear in the second term in the title.
cues.zh: GLM 名稱中有線性，是有原因的。

cues.en: So GLMs and ANOVAs, regressions and correlations, there's a bunch of models that all fall under the same rubric, the same umbrella of GLM.
cues.zh: GLM、ANOVA、迴歸與相關，許多模型都屬於 GLM 的範疇。

cues.en: These are all linear models.
cues.zh: 全部都是線性模型。

cues.en: So, what does linear mean here?
cues.zh: 這裡線性是什麼意思？

cues.en: Linear, in general, and it's sort of the mathematical definition of linear, means scalar multiplication and addition.
cues.zh: 一般而言，線性的數學定義，是純量乘法與加法。

cues.en: So no division, no square root transformations, we just have scalar multiplication.
cues.zh: 沒有除法，也沒有平方根轉換，只有純量乘法。

cues.en: What scalar means is multiplying by a single number.
cues.zh: 純量表示乘上一個數字。

cues.en: So multiplying by a number and adding, those are linear operations and those apply to the regressors.
cues.zh: 乘上一個數字再相加，是線性運算，套用於迴歸變數。

cues.en: So things like logarithms, square roots, powers, trigonometric functions, et cetera, these are all nonlinear operations, so you're not allowed to incorporate these
cues.zh: 對數、平方根、次方、三角函數等等，都是非線性運算，因此不允許把它們納入

cues.en: into the regressors of a general linear model.
cues.zh: 一般線性模型的迴歸變數。

cues.en: Now, the thing is that this, the reason why I'm having this slide here is that people sometimes get a little bit confused about what the linear refers to.
cues.zh: 放這張投影片，是因為人們有時會搞混，線性究竟指什麼。

cues.en: The data themselves can have nonlinearities, there can be nonlinear relationships between the data, it's just that the parameters in the model
cues.zh: 資料本身可以有非線性，資料間可以存在非線性關係，但模型中的參數

cues.en: have to be linear.
cues.zh: 必須是線性的。

cues.en: And that's for the fitting operation, it's the way that these parameters get fit.
cues.zh: 這是針對擬合運算，也就是參數被擬合的方式。

cues.en: As soon as you have nonlinearities in the parameters, then it's no longer a linear model, you have nonlinear models.
cues.zh: 參數一旦有非線性，就不再是線性模型，而是非線性模型。

cues.en: And you'll see examples of that later with logistic regression.
cues.zh: 之後邏輯斯迴歸會看到例子。

cues.en: Sometimes nonlinearities in the data can be linearized.
cues.zh: 有時可以把資料中的非線性線性化。

cues.en: This is not usually done because it's necessary, it's usually done to facilitate the interpretation.
cues.zh: 通常不是因為必要，而是為了方便解讀。

cues.en: Okay, so let me give you an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: Here is our new model.
cues.zh: 這是新的模型。

cues.en: So now we have beta one, which is a regressor, divided by the natural log of beta two, and all of that cubed, all that to the power of three.
cues.zh: beta1 這個迴歸項，除以 beta2 的自然對數，再把整個量立方，也就是三次方。

cues.en: So look at all these ridiculous nonlinearities in here.
cues.zh: 看看裡面這些誇張的非線性。

cues.en: These are totally, totally unacceptable, these are nonlinearities.
cues.zh: 完全不能接受，這些都是非線性。

cues.en: These do not fit into a general linear model framework.
cues.zh: 不符合一般線性模型的架構。

cues.en: On the other hand, here we have a multiplication, so we're just multiplying sex by parents' height.
cues.zh: 另一方面，這裡是乘法，把性別乘以父母身高。

cues.en: This is actually totally fine, this is acceptable.
cues.zh: 這完全可以接受。

cues.en: In fact, this is how you get an interaction in a regression.
cues.zh: 事實上，這就是迴歸中建立交互作用的方式。

cues.en: So in the previous section with ANOVAs, you learned how to compute interaction terms and how to interpret interaction terms.
cues.zh: 上一單元 ANOVA 已學過如何計算與解讀交互作用項。

cues.en: In a regression, you can also have interactions, and the interpretation is the same.
cues.zh: 迴歸也可以有交互作用，而且解讀相同。

cues.en: So let's say maybe your parents' height is only important if you are a man, and if you're a woman, then it doesn't matter how tall your parents are,
cues.zh: 例如父母身高，可能只有男性才重要；女性則不論父母有多高，

cues.en: that doesn't affect how tall you are going to be.
cues.zh: 都不會影響她的身高。

cues.en: So that would be an example of an interaction term.
cues.zh: 這就是交互作用項的一個例子。

cues.en: So this is acceptable because this is just regular multiplication.
cues.zh: 可以接受，因為只是一般乘法。

cues.en: Here we have nonlinearities on the regression terms, on the beta parameters, so this is not acceptable for a linear model.
cues.zh: 這裡則對迴歸項、beta 參數施加非線性，所以線性模型不能接受。

cues.en: All right, so this was a pretty productive video.
cues.zh: 這支影片很有收穫。

cues.en: I gave you an introduction into the general linear model and set you up to learn more about the details of regression.
cues.zh: 介紹了一般線性模型，讓你準備好學習更詳細的迴歸內容。

cues.en: Over the next several videos, I'm going to get more into the math and the mechanisms behind computing regression analyses.
cues.zh: 接下來幾支影片，會更深入迴歸分析計算背後的數學與機制。
